image_description: A museum exhibit featuring the fossilized skeleton of a Triceratops. The image shows the skull with its characteristic three horns and large frill, along with the ribcage, spine, and partial limb bones mounted on a metal armature. The background includes other exhibits and museum infrastructure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeletal mount clearly displays the two large brow horns and the smaller nasal horn in the correct anatomical positions.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a skeletal mount; the keratinous beak (rhamphotheca) is soft tissue and does not preserve in fossils, so it is absent from the image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible limb bones (humerus, femur) are thick and columnar, consistent with a weight-bearing quadrupedal stance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The parietal-squamosal frill is massive and clearly extends well beyond the width of the facial portion of the skull.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears as solid bone plates without large fenestrations (holes), typical of Triceratops, and shows marginal undulations.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: As a skeletal mount, no skin or soft tissue impressions are visible in this specific view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mounting posture shows the shoulders lower than the hips, consistent with the anatomical difference in limb length.
The caudal vertebrae visible behind the pelvis are robust and taper quickly, matching the 'short and stout' description.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic identity of the dinosaur skeleton and distinguish it from other ceratopsians.
To verify the 3D coherence of the complex overlapping bones and ensure the background museum elements do not bleed into the foreground subject.
To check for any AI-generated fusion artifacts between the individual bones or between the skeleton and the support armature.

focus_areas: Anatomical correctness of the horn arrangement
Separation between skeleton and background/mounting hardware
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Verify if the skeletal proportions match real-world Triceratops fossils. Pay close attention to the junction between the skull and the neck vertebrae for any unnatural blending. Ensure the background details (museum walls/other exhibits) maintain consistent perspective and do not show warping.
